title: Give the sign-in front its place in a private PIM database
purpose: Gives the PIM Manager's sign-in front exactly what it needs in the PIM database: a database user for the front's managed identity, the schema 'signin' owned by it, and the right to create tables there. It never adds a role. -WhatIf shows it first; running it again changes nothing.
whenToRun: Once, on a PRIVATE installation (the SQL server has no public endpoint) that is moved onto the sign-in front, when the move or support says the front's database place is missing. Run it from a machine inside the PIM network. Public installations get this from the installation by themselves.

runAs.name: A database owner: a member of the SQL admin group (grp-pim-sql-admins) or the server's Microsoft Entra administrator
runAs.why: Creates the database user and the schema and grants CREATE TABLE.

runAs.name: browser sign-in (your own account; an Azure Arc / VM machine identity on this computer is ignored), or the Invardia Support app's session in this window
runAs.why: No Azure CLI, no PowerShell module, no certificate, no secret on the command line.

changes.object: a database user for the sign-in front's managed identity, created from its client id (CREATE USER ... WITH SID, TYPE = E) when no user has that id
changes.scope: the one PIM database (-SqlDatabase, default PimPlatform)
changes.why: The front signs in to the database as its managed identity.
changes.undo: DROP USER [<identity name>] in the PIM database (after DROP SCHEMA signin and its tables).

changes.object: the schema 'signin', owned by that user (or its owner moved to that user)
changes.permission: owner of the schema signin only
changes.why: The front keeps its sessions, token cache and key ring in two tables it creates in this schema; it can read and change nothing else.
changes.undo: Drop the tables in schema signin, then DROP SCHEMA signin.

changes.permission: CREATE TABLE (database level; usable only in the schema it owns)
changes.why: The front creates its two tables itself on first start.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant id. The sign-in is pinned to it.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The subscription of the PIM SQL server.

parameters.name: SqlServerName
parameters.help: The SQL server name or its FQDN (sql-x or sql-x.database.windows.net).

parameters.name: IdentityName
parameters.help: The sign-in front's managed identity name (the database user's name).

parameters.name: IdentityClientId
parameters.help: The sign-in front's managed identity client id (the database user's SID).

readsOnly: the database user with the identity's client id, the owner of schema signin and the CREATE TABLE grant, before and after the change
network: the PIM SQL server on port 1433 (from inside the PIM network)
localhost (the browser returns the sign-in to a local port on this computer)
whatIf: Signs in, connects, prints the user, the schema owner and the grant as they are now, and the statements it would run. Nothing is changed.
undo: In the PIM database: drop the tables in schema signin, DROP SCHEMA signin, REVOKE CREATE TABLE and DROP USER for the front's identity. The front then cannot keep sign-ins.
